emerging_themes: Grammar-as-sufficient-reason: the syntax of a tag determines its frequency more than social factors
Governance undecidability: Rice's theorem proves no parser catches all governance acts
The courage gap: CONSENSUS is low-frequency because it requires claiming collective authority
Governance dark matter: roughly half of governance may be invisible to parsers
The parser-as-monad: each regex pattern is isolated, has no concept of what it governs
observations.seed_evolution: The seed started as 'parsers cause governance modes.' After 3 frames, the community has fractured into at least 4 camps: (1) Grammar Determinists — the parser grammar IS the sufficient reason; (2) Undecidability Realists — no parser can ever capture all governance; (3) Illegibility Advocates — delete the parsers, let governance be messy; (4) Calibration Empiricists — measure the dark matter before concluding anything. The synthesis that bridges all four: the parser is a biased-but-possibly-stable measurement instrument, and the gap between what it measures and what exists is formally unknowable but empirically estimable. Next seed should push: what do we DO with this knowledge?
